title: Scheduling a Report by Email with a Custom Subject and Body in SAP SuccessFactors
author: AMIT_SHARMA01
text:
Introduction 
 Many business teams need a report delivered to their inbox on a fixed schedule rather than logging in to run it manually. In SAP SuccessFactors, this can be achieved using the Report Distributor, which lets you bundle one or more reports, choose recipients, define your own email subject and message, and run the whole thing on a schedule. 
 In this blog post, I will walk you through the end-to-end steps to schedule a report by email with a customised email subject and body, with screenshots for each step. 
 Step-by-Step Configuration 
 Step 1: Open Report Centre and go to View Schedules 
 Navigate to Report Centre and click View Schedules in the top-right corner of the page. Report Centre – View Schedules Report Centre – View Schedules 
 Step 2: Switch to the legacy Report Distributor tool 
 On the View Schedules page, click Switch to the legacy Report Distributor Tool . 
 Switch to the legacy Report Distributor Tool Switch to the legacy Report Distributor Tool 
 Step 3: Create a new bundle 
 Click New Bundle and provide the following details: 
 Bundle Name – a meaningful name for your scheduled report. 
 Page Size – for example, LETTER. 
 Export Type / Export Format – the output file type of the attachment (for example PDF or Excel) will depend on the option you select here. 
 Click OK to create the bundle. Add New Bundle Add New Bundle 
 Step 4: Add the report to the bundle 
 Click on your newly created bundle in the list, then click Add Item and select Add Report . Select the new bundle and click Add Item Select the new bundle and click Add Item Add Item options: Add Report, Add Excel Table, Add CSV Table Add Item options: Add Report, Add Excel Table, Add CSV Table 
 In the report tree, expand All reports not in this bundle and select ReportCenter (or any other section) to find your report. Expand All reports not in this bundle and select ReportCenter Expand All reports not in this bundle and select ReportCenter 
 Select the required report and click Add . The report is now added to the bundle. Choose the report from the list Choose the report from the list The report now appears in the bundle’s Item List The report now appears in the bundle’s Item List 
 Step 5: Add recipients 
 Open the Recipients tab, click Add Recipients , search for the user(s) who should receive the email, select them and click Add . 
 Search for and add the recipients 
 Step 6: Customise the email (Edit E-mail) 
 Click the bundle name, then select File from the menu at the top left and choose Edit E-mail . File > Edit E-mail 
 By default, the Default message option is selected. To use your own content, select the Override for <Bundle Name> option. You can also add localisations for the languages enabled in your system by using the language selector. 

 Override option and language (localisation) selector 
 Enter the From Address Prefix , the Subject for E-mail and the Body of message . You can personalise the content using these tokens: 
 [%USERNAME%] 
 [%FULLNAME%] 
 [%EMAIL%] Custom email subject and body using tokens 
 Once done, click Submit . 
 Step 7: Schedule the report 
 Go to the Schedule tab and click Add . 

 Schedule tab – Add 
 Enter the start date, start time and how often the schedule should recur (One Time, Daily, Weekly or Monthly), then click OK. The schedule is added and the report is now scheduled. 

 Scheduler – start date, time and frequency 

 Result 
 At the scheduled date and time, the recipients receive an email with your custom subject and message, with the report attached in the export format you selected when creating the bundle. 
 Email received by the recipient with the report attached 
 Conclusion 
 Using the Report Distributor, you can automate report delivery with a personalised email and a recurring schedule, saving users from running reports manually. I hope this post helps you set up scheduled report emails in your own system. Feel free to share your questions or experiences in the comments.

title: The New Kid on the Block in SAP's Integration Portfolio: SAP Managed File Transfer by Redwood
author: Manuel_Namyslo
text:
TechEd is now over – and I am quite happy that we got to experience so many different announcements, sessions and demo exercises related to SAP Integration Suite. If you missed any of it, my colleague Claire has pulled everything together on-demand in this blog post . 
 But one of the greatest things released in recent weeks, which deserves it’s own spotlight is the announcement that SAP Managed File Transfer by Redwood is an SAP Solution Extension . To make sure this news doesn't get lost in the jungle of post-TechEd content, we're hosting a dedicated Activation Webinar on it – and registration is already open here! 
 But just to set the stage: what is SAP Managed File Transfer, and why should you consider it? 
 File transfer - a stubborn gap in enterprise integration 
 Large files, strict audit requirements and external partners still make file transfer one of the most stubborn gaps in enterprise integration – and often the one that holds up an S/4HANA go-live. 
 Because APIs and events get most of the attention in integration conversations. Yet in almost every SAP landscape, a surprisingly large share of business-critical data still moves as files: such as payment and bank statement files, EDI documents with suppliers and customers, payroll exports, product and pricing catalogs, regulatory submissions and batch extracts for analytics. 
 And these requirements are hard to manage properly: 
 Size and volume. Multi-gigabyte files and high-volume batch runs push message-based integration platforms beyond what they're designed for. 
 Compliance. Regulations such as SOX, HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS require encryption, complete audit trails and defined retention – evidence that ad-hoc FTP servers and scripts rarely provide. 
 External partners. Banks, suppliers, logistics providers and authorities each bring their own protocols, keys and schedules. Onboarding every new partner often means another IT ticket, another script and another server nobody wants to own. 
 In many companies, the result is a patchwork of legacy SFTP servers, scheduled jobs and custom code, with little visibility into what was sent, when and to whom. And this patchwork tends to surface at the worst possible moment: during an S/4HANA transformation. When teams inventory their interfaces, file-based flows often turn out to be the largest and least-documented group – and with SAP Process Orchestration approaching the end of mainstream maintenance, they need a future-proof home. 
 SAP Managed File Transfer by Redwood closes that gap 
 As an SAP Solution Extension – co-sold, co-developed and co-supported by SAP – SAP Managed File Transfer (MFT) by Redwood handles what general-purpose integration platforms aren't built for: multi-gigabyte files, audit retention for SOX, HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS, and partner self-service exchanges that don't need IT for every transfer. 
 Combined with SAP Integration Suite, it covers your full integration architecture under a single SAP relationship.

title: SAP PaPM Cloud Standard Model: What's New as of 2026-11-02?
author: jillahgabog
text:
Hello, SAP Community! 👋 
 November is here, and we're back with another round of What’s New series in SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud Standard Model! 🍂 
 Here's what's new : 
 Joule : Run process instances and check their status through Joule. 
 Teams : Copy an existing team to create a new one. Team names can’t be changed after creation. 
 Environment : Delete nodes and their empty subnodes in a single action. 
 About : Access build details and release information more conveniently. 
 Joule 
 Run Process Instances with Joule 
 Whether it's a monthly closing, cost allocation run or sustainability assessment, running process instances is part of everyday activities in Process Management . Now, you have another way to start these runs: Simply tell Joule which process instance you want to run. 
 Joule identifies the process instance based on your request and helps you initiate the run. If multiple activities are available, Joule asks you which one to run before proceeding. 
 To get started, open Joule, switch to Act mode, and enter a request such as: 
 “Run the process instance 'ESG_OCT ’.” 
 “Run all pending process instances for cost center 'EMEA' .” 

 The same authorization rules in Process Management continue to apply. If you don’t have the required permissions or these conditions aren’t met, the run cannot be started. 
 You can also ask Joule for an update on the run status. Joule can inform you whether the run is queued, still running, or completed. 
 For more information, see Joule in Process Management . 
 Teams 
 Why Start from Scratch? 
 Creating teams with similar configurations across departments, regions, or projects no longer means setting up each one from scratch. 
 In the Teams application, you can now copy an existing team to create a new one with similar settings. Team names are also fixed after creation, helping maintain consistent team identities. Copy an Existing Team 
 Simply copy an existing team, give the new team a unique name, and adjust the details as needed. Users assigned to the original team are also copied to the new team. 
 To copy a team: 
 Select an existing team. 
 Choose Create > Copy Team . 
 Enter a unique name for the new team. 

 Optionally, update the description and child teams. 
 Choose Copy . 
 The new team is created with the copied settings, including any changes you made in the dialog. The original team remains unchanged. Team Names Stay Fixed After Creation 
 As part of this enhancement, team names can no longer be changed after creation. The Name field is now read-only when editing an existing team. 

 Teams may already be assigned as performers or reviewers in activities or configured as authorized teams within environments. Keeping team names unchanged provides a stable reference across these assignments. 
 For more information, see Teams . 
 Environment 
 A Simpler Way to Delete Nodes and Their Subnodes 
 In the Environment application, you can now delete a node together with all its subnodes in a single action, as long as none of them contains an environment. 
 Previously, you had to remove each empty subnode before deleting the parent node. Now, you can clear the entire branch at once. 🤩 
 Just remember: If any subnodes contain an environment, you need to delete that environment first. 
 For more information, see Environment . 
 About 
 Access Build Details and Release Information 
 The About dialog in SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud Standard Model now provides faster access to the latest product updates and key application information. 

 With this enhancement, you can: 
 Check the Fast Track Mode status directly in the About dialog. 
 Copy current build details that can be used when working with support. 
 Open the latest release information through the What's New link. 
 The updated layout organizes technical and release-related information into dedicated sections, making it easier to find the details you need from a single location. 
 For more information, see About . 
 For more updates, head over to What's New on SAP Help Portal or catch up on previous SAP Community posts with #PaPMCloudSMWhatsNew . 
 Until next time, see you in the next What’s New! 👋

title: SAP PaPM Cloud Universal Model What’s New as of 2026-11-02
author: KrisReyes
text:
Hello SAP Community, 
 Smarter shortcuts, quicker insights, and a smoother way to work are here! 
 The latest enhancements in SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud Universal Model are all about making everyday tasks simpler and more intuitive. Whether you’re interacting with Joule, checking activities, adapting your UI, or exploring report data, there are new ways to get where you need to go with less effort. 
 Let’s start with Joule. 

 Get started with Slash Commands in Joule 
 Imagine starting with a business requirement rather than an already configured finance environment. 
 You know what the solution needs to achieve, but turning those requirements into a structured design, creating the necessary finance content, building the environment, and then checking the result can involve several stages. 
 With the new finance slash commands in Joule, you can approach this as one guided journey in SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud Universal Model. 
 Ready to Try It? 
 Open Joule in Universal Model, enter “/” in the conversation panel to display all available commands, and choose the finance command that matches where you are on your journey. You can also type the command directly if you already know which action you want to start. 

 Taken together, the new slash commands provide a clear path through the different stages of working with a finance environment such as: 
 /fin-design turns your finance requirements into a blueprint without changing the Universal Model environment. 
 /fin-create creates the required finance content from the approved requirements and blueprint. 
 /fin-build builds the finance environment based on the approved blueprint. 
 /fin-validate checks the resulting environment for completeness and consistency and provides a validation report without changing it. 
 Instead of treating Joule only as a place to ask questions, you can now start a specific finance-related action simply by choosing the appropriate slash command. The commands represent a distinct stage in the process design, so you always know where you are and what comes next. For more information about the prompting recommendations, see Prompting Recommendations 

 Explore your report data more naturally with Ask Joule 

 When working with data in a report, you often know the information you want to see, but getting there can involve several configuration steps. You may need to apply filters, sort your data, create groups, or define aggregations before the grid shows the perspective you need. 
 With the new Ask Joule feature in Insert Show Element , you can take a more conversational approach. 
 Instead of configuring each setting manually, you can tell Joule what you want to do with the data using natural language. Joule then applies the result directly to the grid, helping you transition from a question to the view you need with less manual configuration. 
 For example, instead of manually arranging the grid, you could ask Joule to: 
 filter the information you want to focus on, 
 sort the displayed data, 
 organize information into groups, or 
 aggregate values for analysis. 

 And speaking of getting things done faster, let’s move from smarter interactions to quicker navigation. 

 Quick access to Event Logs and Rules Screen from Manage Activities 
 Working with activities often involves checking event logs or reviewing the rules associated with an activity. Previously, accessing this information required you to open an activity first and navigate to the corresponding link in the activity details. 
 With the latest enhancement of the Manage Activities application, you can now access the Event Logs and Rules screens directly from the activity overview. They will be displayed in new browser tabs. This reduces navigation and makes it easier to review activity-related information while staying within your list of activities. 
 You can add the Event Logs and Rules screen columns to the activity overview using Settings. 
 From the activity overview, you can: 
 Select the Event Logs link to open the event logs in a new browser tab filtered by the respective activity ID. 
 Select the Rules screen link to quickly access the corresponding activity Rules screen in a new tab. The link is available only for activities where the Enable Show Rules checkbox is marked. 
 This enhancement makes frequently used information more accessible and helps streamline activity review and troubleshooting without needing to open each activity individually. 

 Finally, let’s wrap things up with more flexibility in how you work with your data. 

 Apply conditions to multiple columns with ease in Adapt UI 
 Imagine you’re working with a Data screen and want several columns to follow the same condition. Perhaps you want a group of Key Figures to stand out with the same color, or you want to apply the same condition across several Characteristic fields. 
 With the latest Adapt UI enhancement, you can now select multiple columns and apply the condition to them all at once – saving time and keeping your Data screen consistent. 
 Start right from your Data screen 
 There’s no need to leave the Data screen when you want to work with conditions. You can apply a condition to multiple fields and add a color, making the relevant data easier to recognize immediately. 

 Changed your mind? No problem. 
 For example, you can select only the Key Figure fields and remove their color condition, while leaving the conditions applied to the other selected fields unchanged. This lets you refine your Data screen as your needs change. 

 Bring your data back to its original view 
 When you no longer need the conditions, simply select the affected fields, clear the conditions, and save your changes. The conditions are removed, returning the fields to their original state. 

 Whether you want to highlight important information, fine-tune your selections, or start fresh, multiple selections, the Adapt UI feature gives you the flexibility to adjust several fields together instead of working through them one at a time. For more information about the Adapt UI configuration, see Adapt UI 
 And that’s a wrap on these latest enhancements! 
 From smarter interactions with Joule and quicker access to the information you need, to more flexibility in adapting your UI, these updates are designed to make your everyday experience in SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud, Universal Model simpler, faster, and more intuitive. 
 We hope these enhancements help you spend less time navigating and more time focusing on what matters most in your work. 
 Give them a try and discover how they can make a difference in your day-to-day tasks! 
 Thanks for reading, and stay tuned for more updates!

title: Your MCP server is open for contributions, but do your users and their agents know about it?
author: dellagustin
text:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers are essential building blocks in agentic engineering scenarios. The MCP protocol is used in the architecture of AI-native or AI-enabled software solutions, and also by the developers building and maintaining said solutions. 
 What happens though, when the MCP server is not working as expected? What if a feature is missing? Can the MCP client, usually an agent harness, guide its user into finding support and/or feedback channels, or even the contribution guidelines of the project behind the server, when it is open source / InnerSource? Can it contribute bug fixes or missing features? The answer is: No, unless the server is prepared for that. 
 In this blog post you will find the results of an experiment with a demo MCP server created to show a proof-of-concept for enabling such MCP server "introspection" scenarios. The post explains how it works, and takes you to the source code of the demo server, so that you can test it by yourself!

text:
Most organizations are not struggling to invest in AI. They are struggling to see a return on it. Budgets have been committed, projects launched, and expectations set—yet for the majority, the business case remains unproven. 

 This is the context in which SAP redesigned the SAP Services and Support portfolio eight months ago. It’s built around a simple premise: transformation isn’t a milestone but a continuous journey, and every organization deserves a partner to guide it at every stage.

Max Success Plan now helps close the loop—the same complete, tiered path to value that SAP has offered directly since February 2026 is now available to every customer, regardless of how they choose to engage with SAP. 

 The evidence: why guidance determines who wins with AI 

 The data on this is stark. RAND Corporation found that 80% of enterprise AI initiatives fail to deliver their intended business value—twice the failure rate of standard IT projects. S&P Global Market Intelligence found that 42% of companies abandoned most of their AI initiatives in 2025, up from 17% the year before. And MIT’s widely cited GenAI Divide report found that 95% of organizations investing in generative AI see zero measurable return on their P&L, while that same research found that pairing AI adoption with an experienced external partner roughly doubles deployment success, 66% versus 33% for internal-only efforts. 

 The differentiator isn’t the technology stack. It’s guided execution. 

 This is exactly the gap success plans were built to close. They are SAP’s cloud engagement model : the structured, continuous guidance customers have been asking for, helping organizations adopt the latest innovations and stay ready for whatever comes next. And Max Success Plan, as SAP’s most strategic level of engagement, can be that experienced external partner the research points to, built directly into the SAP relationship, not bolted on beside it. 

 The proof: what success plans actually deliver 

 IDC’s research found that organizations using Foundational Success Plan achieved $4.9 million in average annual benefits, 28% less time spent on incident management, and a 39% reduction in impactful security breaches*. Advanced Success Plan customers saw a 381% three-year ROI, $3.4 million in annual average benefits, and 19% quicker time to market for new features and functions**. And Max Success Plan customers achieved a 521% three-year ROI, $4.4 million in end-user productivity gains per organization per year, and a 24% improvement in business processes***. 

 Guidance that pays for itself—at every level. Full findings for each success plan are available on sap.com .

 When SAP introduced the success plans, the goal was clear: give every SAP cloud customer a clear, predictable path to value, one plan included with every subscription and two additional that scale with ambition. What became apparent almost immediately was how many of those customers already reach SAP through a partner—and how natural the next question was: why should the path to value look any different because of that? 

 Extending Max Success Plan through partner channels closes a gap that had nothing to do with the value of the offering and everything to do with how customers happened to reach it. That relationship should no longer determine the level of guidance available.

By making Max Success Plan available through our partner channels, we are expanding access to the expertise and support customers need to turn innovation into lasting business value.” 
 Thomas Saueressig, Chief Customer Officer and Member of the Executive Board of SAP SE 

 Max Success Plan: strategic guidance, built into every engagement 

 Max Success Plan is SAP’s most comprehensive success plan, designed for organizations navigating complex transformations, scaling SAP Business AI, or operating in fast-moving business environments. It combines strategic expertise, proactive guidance, and hands-on support to help customers continuously evolve and maximize the value of their SAP investments.

 This phased approach reflects a key insight since February: the organizations that get the most from success plans are those that adopt at a pace matching their own readiness. 

 As SAP builds toward the Autonomous Enterprise , where AI increasingly supports execution while people set the direction and hold accountability, the guidance layer around that technology matters as much as the technology itself. Expanding Max Success Plan across partner models gives more customers access to the strategic guidance they need to adopt innovation, navigate continuous transformation, and realize greater value from their SAP investments. 

 The guidance is in place. The next step is yours. 

 The difference between an AI initiative that transforms a business and one that quietly stalls is rarely the technology. It is the guidance around it—the expertise that connects a product roadmap to a business outcome and keeps that connection strong as both evolve.

title: S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition (009) - RISE環境から外部システムへHTTP(S)でアクセスする方法(Squid Proxy Allowlist)
author: KevinYin
text:
SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Editionにおいて、RISE側のサーバからインターネット経由で外部システムへHTTP(S)方式でアクセスしたいケースがあるかと存じます。なお、本記事は、お客様が ご利用のPlatformがCloud(AWS/Azure/GCP)であることを前提 に記載しております。 
 その際に利用するのが、下記のService Request(以下、SR)です。 
 SRテンプレート: Allowlist Squid Proxy access HTTP/HTTPS(80/443): OUTBOUND to EXTERNAL 
 反対に、外部システムからインターネット経由でRISE側のサーバへアクセスしたい場合は、RISE側にLoadBalancerを設置し、システムをインターネットに公開する必要があります。LoadBalancerを作成する場合は、下記のSRテンプレートをご利用ください。 
 SRテンプレート: Create Hyperscaler LB for INBOUND traffic from an EXTERNAL source (Azure/AWS/GCP) 
 SRを起票される前に、下記の点をご認識いただけますようお願いいたします。 
 SRを起票する前に、インターネット経由でのアクセス先を確認し、現状アクセスできていないことをご確認ください。なお、動的に変更されるIPアドレスは、Squid Proxyのホワイトリストに追加しないようお願いいたします。IPアドレスが動的に変更されるため、変更された時点でアクセスできなくなります。 
 本作業はシステムを停止せずに実施でき、業務への影響(ダウンタイム)は発生いたしません。 
 SRのサービス説明に記載されているとおり、本SRは基本的にSIDごとではなく、CID単位で一度のみ申請してください。 
 リクエストはSIDごとではなく、ネットワークセグメントごとに1件提出するだけで十分です。SIDを選択すると、SAPは関連するCSN(Customer Secure Network)またはCGS(Customer Gateway Service)ノードを特定し、そのノードにプロキシ設定を適用します。プロキシはネットワーク層で動作するため、同一のCSN/CGSノードに接続されているすべてのSAPシステムが同じ設定を継承します。 
 補足として、Squid ProxyはCSNまたはCGS上で稼働しており、内部で冗長化されています。なお、障害などにより切り替えが発生した際には、セッションが引き継がれない点をご認識いただけますようお願いいたします。 
 以下では、現時点で提供されている4つの"CIFS Operations"をもとにご説明いたします。 
 Domain Name : To enter your preferred Domain Name in "Enter Domain Name" field. 
 FQDN (Fully Qualified Domain Name) : To enter your preferred FQDN in "Enter FQDN (Fully Qualified Domain Name)" field. 
 IP Address : To enter your preferred IP Address in "Enter IP Address" field. 
 IP Address Range : To enter your preferred IP Address Range in "Enter IP Address Range" field. 
 Domain Name 
 Input Typeにて"Domain Name"を選択し、必要なドメイン名を入力してください。必要に応じて、一度に複数のドメイン名を入力することも可能です。 

 ドメイン名sap.com（ドットなし）は、sap.comのみへのアクセスが許可されます。 
 ドメイン名.amazon.com（ドットあり）は、そのドメインおよびすべてのサブドメインが許可されます。 
 例えば、下記のようなFQDNへのアクセスが可能となります。 
 aws.amazon.com 
 signin.aws.amazon.com 
 ap-northeast-1.signin.aws.amazon.com 
 アクセスを許可したいドメイン名にドットが必要な場合は、明確に記載いただけますようお願いいたします。 
 FQDN 
 Input Typeにて"FQDN (Fully Qualified Domain Name)"を選択し、必要なFQDNを入力してください。必要に応じて、一度に複数のFQDNを入力することも可能です。 

 上記の場合、本SR対応完了後に、下記のFQDNへのアクセスが許可されます。 
 www.sap.com 
 dc.services.visualstudio.com 
 IP Address 
 Input Typeにて"IP Address"を選択し、必要なIPアドレスを入力してください。必要に応じて、一度に複数のIPアドレスを入力することも可能です。 

 前述のとおり、IPアドレスをホワイトリストに追加する場合は、動的に変更されるIPアドレスを避けていただけますようお願いいたします。IPアドレスレンジが分かっている場合は"IP Address Range"をご利用いただき、変更される可能性のあるIPアドレスが複数ある場合は、すべてのIPアドレスを申請してください。 
 IP Address Range 
 Input Typeにて"IP Address Range"を選択し、必要なIPアドレスレンジを入力してください。必要に応じて、一度に複数のIPアドレスレンジを入力することも可能です。 

 まとめ 
 本記事では、RISE側のサーバからHTTP(S)プロトコルを利用し、インターネット経由で外部システムと連携する際に必要となるSRの申請方法についてご紹介しました。アクセス先の指定方法には、Domain Name、FQDN、IP Address、IP Address Rangeの4つのInput Typeがあり、要件に応じて使い分けていただくことが可能です。 
 申請にあたっては、事前にアクセス先と現状を確認すること、動的に変更されるIPアドレスはホワイトリストに追加しないこと、そしてCID単位で一度のみ申請することがポイントとなります。本記事が、RISE環境における外部システム連携の設定を進める際の一助となれば幸いです。

title: How We Built a Smart Document Archival Solution for SAP SuccessFactors HCM Using SAP HANA Cloud
author: KavyaManohara
text:
Introduction 
 In many organizations, employee documents are maintained across multiple HR systems and legacy applications. During migrations to SAP SuccessFactors HCM, preserving these historical documents and ensuring their continued accessibility can become a challenge. 
 Documents such as employee records, certificates, tax documents, and other HR-related files need to be retained for future reference. Managing these documents manually or accessing them through legacy systems can be time-consuming and difficult. 
 To address this challenge, we developed a Document Archival Solution for SAP SuccessFactors HCM using SAP HANA Cloud , providing a centralized approach to migrate employee documents from different HR systems, store them in SAP HANA Cloud, and access them through SAP SuccessFactors. 
 Our Approach 
 We built the solution on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) , leveraging SAP HANA Cloud as the central repository for archived employee documents. 
 The solution simplifies document migration and archival by transferring documents from different HR systems into SAP HANA Cloud while maintaining their association with employee records. Users can then access and view archived documents through SAP SuccessFactors. 
 Legacy HR Systems → Document Migration → SAP HANA Cloud → SAP SuccessFactors → Document Retrieval 

 Solution Overview 
 The solution provides a centralized approach to migrate and manage employee documents from different HR systems. Documents are transferred from source systems and stored in SAP HANA Cloud, where they are maintained for archival purposes. Users can access and view these archived documents directly through SAP SuccessFactors, simplifying document retrieval and management.

 Key Features and Benefits 
 1. Document Migration 
 The solution supports the migration of employee documents from different HR systems and legacy applications into the archival environment. Users can select the required documents and initiate the migration process. 
 Business Benefit: Simplifies document migration from multiple source systems and brings historical employee documents into a centralized environment. 
 2. Document Upload and SAP HANA Cloud Storage 
 The solution provides an upload capability to transfer employee documents into SAP HANA Cloud for centralized archival. Users can provide the required document details, select the files, and upload them to the archival repository. 
 Business Benefit: Enables centralized document storage and simplifies the management of archived employee records. 

 Figure 2: Load Documents – Document Upload and Storage 

 3. Access Archived Documents from SAP SuccessFactors 
 The solution enables users to access archived employee documents through SAP SuccessFactors. This provides a convenient way to retrieve documents stored in the archival repository without depending on the original legacy systems. 
 Business Benefit: Improves document accessibility by bringing archived employee records closer to the HR system used by the organization. 
 4. View and Retrieve Archived Documents 
 Users can search for archived documents using relevant information such as Employee ID, module, and document category. The application displays the matching documents along with their associated details, allowing users to view and retrieve the required files. 
 Business Benefit: Simplifies document search and helps HR users quickly locate historical employee records. 

 Figure 3: View Archived Documents – Search and Retrieval 

 5. Categorized Employee Documents 
 The My Documents section provides an organized view of employee documents across different categories, including Resume, Educational Background, Certifications, Offer Documents, Tax Documents, Work Permit, and Passport. 
 This categorization helps users identify and access the required documents based on their document type. 
 Business Benefit: Improves document organization and makes employee-related information easier to locate and access.

 The solution delivers business value by simplifying employee document archival while addressing document retention and operational challenges. 

 It preserves historical employee documents during HR system migrations and legacy system retirements, ensuring important records remain available for future reference. 

 It centralizes document storage in SAP HANA Cloud, reducing dependency on multiple disconnected repositories. 

 It improves accessibility by enabling HR users to access and view archived employee documents directly through SAP SuccessFactors. 

 It reduces manual effort by providing a structured process for document migration, upload, categorization, and retrieval. 

 Finally, it supports audit readiness and efficient document management by keeping historical employee records organized, searchable, and accessible when required. 
 Conclusion 
 The Document Archival Solution brings together document migration, transfer, archival storage, synchronization, and retrieval into a centralized application. 
 By integrating SAP SuccessFactors HCM with SFTP-based document transfer and SAP HANA Cloud for archival storage, the solution provides a structured approach to managing employee documents throughout their archival lifecycle. 
 It helps organizations simplify document migration, reduce manual effort, improve document accessibility, and maintain historical employee records in an organized manner. Users can access and retrieve archived documents through SAP SuccessFactors whenever required, reducing dependency on legacy HR systems.

title: S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition (008) - APサーバからお客様のCIFSサーバ上の共有フォルダをマウントする方法
author: KevinYin
text:
SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Editionにおいて、APサーバからCIFSを利用し、お客様側のオンプレミス環境、またはお客様所有のCloud上のCIFSサーバ上のファイルへアクセスする方法についてご紹介いたします。 
 構成を整理いたしますと、以下のとおりとなります。 
 RISE側のAPサーバ: CIFSクライアント 

 お客様オンプレミス/お客様所有のCloud上のサーバ: CIFSサーバ 
 ご利用するService Request(以下、SR)テンプレートは、下記のとおりでございます。 
 SRテンプレート: Mount CIFS (aka Samba) shares 
 SRを起票される前に、下記の前提条件をご確認いただけますようお願いいたします。 
 RISE上のAPサーバからのみ、お客様所有のCIFSサーバをマウントできること(HANAサーバでのCIFSマウントは許可されておりません)。そのため、SRを作成される際は、SIDとしてAPサーバをご選択いただくこととなります。 
 RISE上のAPサーバと、お客様オンプレミス/お客様所有のCloud上のサーバ間でネットワーク通信が可能であること。 
 RISE側のAP(CIFSクライアント)から、CIFSサーバのポート139または445へアクセスできること(現状は、基本的にポート445が使用されます)。 
 CIFSマウントポイントの数は、1台のAPサーバ上で5つまでとなるよう設計いただくことを推奨いたします。 
 以下では、現時点で提供されている4つの"CIFS Operations"をもとにご説明いたします。 
 Create: Mount new customer CIFS shares on Linux hosts 
 Modify: Unmounts existing CIFS shares and Remount with modified details 
 Remount: Unmount and remount existing CIFS shares (without modifications) 
 Unmount: Unmount or cleanup existing CIFS shares 

 新規CIFSマウントの作成 

 新規でCIFSマウントポイントを作成する場合に利用いたします。 
 下記は、CIFSサーバ10.218.3.20の共有名sharenameを、該当サーバの/mnt/smbshareにマウントする例でございます。 

 Customer Domain Name : "CIFS User Name"でご指定いただくユーザがドメイン上に存在する場合は、ドメイン名をご指定ください。それ以外の場合はWORKGROUPとなります。 
 CIFS Share Name : 共有名をご指定ください。例えば、あるフォルダに対して共有設定を実施した後に設定した共有名となります。 
 CIFS User Name : CIFSクライアントからCIFSサーバへアクセスする際のユーザ名となります。 
 Is PASSWORD updated in Customer Logon Depot?: CIFSユーザのパスワードをLogon Depotに保存のうえ、チェックを入れてください。ご不明な場合は、SAP Notes 1773689をご参照ください。 
 Target Hostname(s) : RISE側のAPサーバのホスト名をご指定ください。複数のご指定が可能です。 
 Checking PORT access to CIFS Server : "TCP ports 445/139 are reachable, ready to proceed"と表示されることをご確認ください。お客様側で、RISE側のAPサーバからCIFSサーバの139または445ポートへのアクセスを許可いただく必要がございます。 
 Target Mount Point : RISE側APサーバにて、CIFSマウントポイントとなるディレクトリをご指定ください。免責事項に記載のある/install、/tmpなどの配下のディレクトリは利用しないようお願いいたします。 
 Mount Point permissions : 必須項目ではなく、デフォルトのパーミッションは775となります。必要に応じてご指定ください。 
 Share Owner : 必須項目ではなく、デフォルトのユーザグループはsidadm:sapsysとなります。通常は変更いただく必要はございませんが、特定の要件がある場合はご指定ください。 

 CIFSマウントの設定変更 

 既存のCIFSマウントの設定を変更する場合に利用いたします。 
 CIFSマウント変更の項目は、"Select entity to Modify"パラメータのダイアログボックスからご確認いただけます。下記は、現時点で選択可能な変更項目でございます。 
 CIFS Server details: Customer CIFS server details (ex. IP, FQDN, etc.) 
 Domain Name: Customer side Domain name of the CIFS server 
 CIFS Share Name: Customer side exported CIFS share name 
 CIFS user name: Customer side CIFS user name 
 CIFS password: Customer side CIFS password 
 ECS side Mount point: Modify CIFS mount point on SAP ECS host 
 Share permissions: Modify CIFS mount point permissions on SAP ECS host 
 Change share owner: Modify CIFS mount point owner on SAP ECS host 
 下記は、CIFSサーバへの接続時のパスワードを変更するSRを例としております。 

 CIFS Operations : Modify 
 Select entity to Modify : CIFS password 
 Is PASSWORD updated in Customer Logon Depot? : 変更後のパスワードをCustomer Logon Depotにメンテナンスしたうえで、チェックを入れてください。 
 Target Hostname(s) : CIFSクライアントとして稼働しているRISE上のAPサーバのホスト名をご指定ください(複数のホストをご指定いただけます)。 
 Target Mount Point : RISE上のAPサーバ上のマウントポイントをご指定ください。 
 CIFS mount point? : 上記のすべての項目の入力が完了しましたら、選択項目をクリックし、"Valid CIFS mount, good to preceed"が表示されることをご確認のうえ、クリックしてください。万が一、すべての項目を正しく入力しているにもかかわらず、"Valid CIFS mount, good to preceed"が表示されない場合は、RISEの担当者までご連絡ください。 

 CIFSマウントポイントの再マウント(設定変更なし) 

 既存のCIFSマウントを再マウント(アンマウント/マウント)する場合に利用いたします。 
 下記は、対象サーバ上のCIFSマウントポイント /mnt/smbshare の再マウント依頼の例でございます。 

 CIFS Operations : Remount 
 Target Hostname(s) : 対象サーバのホスト名をリストからご選択ください。 
 Target Mount Point: 該当サーバ上でのCIFSマウントポイントをご入力ください。大文字・小文字を含め、正確にご入力いただく必要がございます。 
 CIFS mount point? : 上記のすべての項目の入力が完了しましたら、選択項目をクリックし、"Valid CIFS mount, good to preceed"が表示されることをご確認のうえ、クリックしてください。万が一、すべての項目を正しく入力しているにもかかわらず、"Valid CIFS mount, good to preceed"が表示されない場合は、RISEの担当者までご連絡ください。 

 CIFSマウントポイントのアンマウント 

 CIFSマウントをアンマウントする場合に利用いたします。 
 下記は、対象サーバ上のCIFSマウントポイント /mnt/smbshare のアンマウント依頼の例でございます。 

 CIFS Operations : Unmount 
 Target Hostname(s) : 対象サーバのホスト名をリストからご選択ください。 
 Target Mount Point : 該当サーバ上でのCIFSマウントポイントをご入力ください。大文字・小文字を含め、正確にご入力いただく必要がございます。 
 CIFS mount point?: 上記のすべての項目の入力が完了しましたら、選択項目をクリックし、"Valid CIFS mount, good to preceed"が表示されることをご確認のうえ、クリックしてください。万が一、すべての項目を正しく入力しているにもかかわらず、"Valid CIFS mount, good to preceed"が表示されない場合は、RISEの担当者までご連絡ください。 

 まとめ 

 本記事では、SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Editionにおいて、CIFSを利用し、お客様側のオンプレミス環境、またはお客様所有のCloud上のCIFSサーバ上の共有フォルダをマウントする方法について、SRテンプレート「Mount CIFS (aka Samba) shares」を用いて、Create/Modify/Remount/Unmountの4つのOperationごとにご紹介いたしました。 
 SRを起票される際は、本記事に記載の前提条件をご確認のうえ、ご対応いただけますと幸いです。本記事が、CIFSマウントの設定を行う際の一助となれば幸いでございます。

title: Substitution in ledger 0L CoCd 1010 failed. Fields: RBUNIT Message No. FINCS_ACCTG_INTEG009

 Substitution in ledger 0L CoCd 1010 failed. Fields: RBUNIT

 Ledger 0L is a Preparation Ledger for Group Reporting, which means fields relevant for group reporting and consolidation-specific fields, such as consolidation unit, are available in general ledger accounting.

 Procedure 
 Review the customizing for the Group Reporting Preparation Ledger, in particular the substitution rules.

 Questions

 The objective is to obtain a balance sheet presentation that distinguishes: 
 Inventory in company-owned warehouses 
 Inventory physically held at customer locations under consignment 
 Any insights, best practices, or references to SAP documentation would be greatly appreciated.

 João

title: SAP Datasphere: Using REPLICATIONFLOW_RUN_DETAILS ($TEC schema) in an SQL View to export delta count

text:
Hello everyone, 
 We use SAP Datasphere to replicate data from SAP S/4HANA to Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS). We replicate about 100 S/4HANA tables, and most replication flows contain several tables. To build that file, we need system information about each run: which replication flows completed successfully with the number of records transferred per table. 

 What we have done so far 

 Database Analysis User: We created a Database Analysis User with Enable Space Schema Access checked. We connected to the SAP HANA Cloud database through Database Explorer.

 Creating an SQL View in Datasphere: We created an SQL View in the Data Builder on the same technical table so we could replicate it to ADLS. Deployment fails with this error: 
 Status 404 is not accepted: "Entities <space>$TEC.REPLICATIONFLOW_RUN_DETAILS cannot be found in the repository Questions 
 Can the REPLICATIONFLOW_RUN_DETAILS table (schema <schema>$TEC) be used in a View or Data Flow in SAP Datasphere? If so, how?

 Thanks in advance for any guidance!

title: F110 Remittance Email Not Triggering | Custom Program ZFAP2011 and FM Z_REMITTANCE_TO_EMAIL_00002040
author: Mynam_Rajendra
text:
Hi Experts, 
 I am working on a requirement related to remittance advice email generation after an F110 payment run. We are working on ecc. 
 Business Requirement 
 The requested changes are: 
 Update the sender email address used in remittance communications. 
 Maintain different email recipient information for multiple company codes. 
 Ensure remittance emails are generated correctly after payment processing. 
 Current Issue 
 The remittance email is not being triggered as expected. 
 The functionality involves custom development that has evolved over several years with multiple enhancements. Due to confidentiality restrictions, I am unable to share program names, function modules, email addresses, company information, or code snippets. 
 Based on an internal technical analysis, we identified that: 
 Sender email addresses are determined through custom logic. 
 Email recipient information is maintained through configuration/text maintenance. 
 Some company code specific email details appear to be fetched dynamically, while others were historically maintained directly in the application logic. 
 The remittance process is triggered after F110/FBPM1 processing. 
 The issue appears to be related to the email generation flow rather than payment run completion.

 Checked ST22 and found no related dumps. 
 Attempted analysis using ST12 traces but could not identify the custom email generation process. 
 Reviewed background jobs in SM37. 
 Investigated email maintenance/configuration used by the remittance process. 
 Confirmed that the issue is related to email triggering rather than payment document creation. 

 What is the recommended approach to identify the exact custom process responsible for remittance email generation after F110? 
 When the process runs in the background, is SM37 + JDBG the preferred debugging approach? 
 Are there standard enhancement points, BADIs, BTEs, Payment Medium Workbench objects, or output-processing components typically involved in remittance email generation that should be investigated? 

 Please help us. To trigger the custom email fm. We tried all other possible ways what we know. So i'm approaching you to receive ideas from you. 

 Any guidance on debugging custom remittance email generation in an F110 payment process would be greatly appreciated. 
 Thanks in advance.

title: The reset usage decision is not appearing for the following inspection lots
author: mineshram
text:
Manage Usage decision 
 The reset usage decision is not appearing for the following inspection lots - SAP suggests the note below. 
 the system status shows UD ICCO SPCO but the Usage Decision field is blank and the Quality Score is 0 — this confirms a status inconsistency where the UD flag was set internally but no actual usage decision data was recorded. This is precisely why the Reset Usage Decision button is not appearing — the app logic requires a recognized UD record to display the reset option
